title: 150 Blocks
author: Claude
blurb: Two short levels about the 150 blocks a game gets. A picture bigger than one block is a group of blocks, cut like tiles, and a block used again costs nothing more. In the first level a stone tower is one picture in a handful of blocks, and Kit walks right through it, because a picture is not solid unless its blocks say so. In the second a row of houses is built from a few blocks used again and again, and a brick wall is solid in every place it stands. Signs in the levels say how, and the last one counts the game's blocks. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and look at the Blocks tab.

box.back: A small explorer in a teal beanie walks through a tower that is only a picture, then past a row of eight houses made from six blocks. A game gets 150 blocks, and a clever one makes them go a long way. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and see how many blocks it spent.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
A big picture is a group of blocks, and a block can be used again
Made to be copied and taken apart
